subject: A hash in a PARENTHESISED list literal is not flattened: my @a = (1,%h,2) yields HASH(0x..) instead of the pairs — silent wrong values
description:
DONE s319 (4c9fd75).  Pre-existing — verified identical at HEAD in a worktree
BEFORE changing anything, so it was not fallout from #169.

SYMPTOM: `my @a = (1, %h, 2)` stored the hash as ONE element (HASH(0x..)) with a
wrong element COUNT.  Silent, value-corrupting, and in an everyday idiom:
`my @pairs = (%defaults, %overrides)`.

THE FLATTEN WAS MISSING IN TWO PLACES — and the second only surfaced because the
regression tests included the INVERSE cases.  After fixing the first, `@a = (…)`
was right while `[…]` was still wrong; without those guards I would have shipped
a half fix:
 1. `p-array-fill`'s vector AND list loops had no hash-table arm, so a hash
    element fell through to the scalar branch.
 2. `p-array-init` — the anonymous ARRAY constructor — had the same gap:
    `[$x,$y,%e,$z]`, `[%f]`.

FIX (CLAUDE.md 11 — no third copy of the maphash): the loops recurse into the
hash-table arm that already sits above them; p-array-init delegates to
%p-flatten-list and lets its own vector arm store the result.  Keying on a RAW
hash-table is what keeps a hash REFERENCE (a p-box) on the scalar arm as one
element — guarded by a test.

CHECKED AND ALREADY CORRECT (do not re-investigate): anon-HASH constructor
{a=>1,%f}; hash-target merge %m=(%a,%b); merge with an empty hash; push; sub
args; `my $n = () = (…)` count context; "@{[ … ]}" interpolation; bare @a=%h.

VERIFIED: gate 124 files / 4459 tests PASS.  Sweep 0 new, 1 blessed row fixed,
and perl-tests/hashassign.t went to ZERO failures — fully-passing files 65 -> 66.
fail-baseline 691 -> 690 by removing exactly the one cleared row.

TEST-FLAKINESS NOTE: perl hash order is undefined and varies BETWEEN RUNS of
perl itself (confirmed: two different orders in three runs).  Every assertion
added for this sorts or counts; never compare raw hash order.

RESIDUE: op/hashassign.t (the t/ original) — recheck; the perl-tests copy is
clean, and t307-309 were failing only on this bug.
